result.scientific_strategy:
## abd93958-a0b2-4d26-b212-96ebeb401d22 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The objective is at least 98% success, or 196 of 200 episodes, on the unchanged official two-joint-arm reach-and-hold task. The fresh baseline reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.0% on the protected task-reference panel at checkpoint-100352, while full-radius transfer in experiment 2 reached 97.0% and 98.5% and remains the strongest measured artifact. Joint shaping, targeted sampling, unchanged continuation, hold-credit forfeiture, a lower transfer learning rate, and sharper closeness shaping did not improve that artifact; two fresh replications instead remained at 62.5-67.5% on both development panels. The campaign therefore has one useful transferred trajectory, poor fresh trajectories, and no robust cross-panel attainment. Experiment 10's sharper local distance signal produced 95.5%/97.0% early, 90.5%/92.0% late, and 94.5%/95.5% at the endpoint on the researcher/task-reference panels, respectively, all below the retained parent. Reward curvature is weakened as an explanation under this transferred recipe, while action control, policy capacity, and PPO trajectory effects remain unresolved. This is provisional memory for reassessment and prescribes no next action.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, not logged reward or training success, is the policy-progress signal. Checkpoint and trajectory choice matter: several experiments showed proxy or late-training gains without task improvement. Full-radius transfer recovered two short-radius negative-angle failures from experiment 1, but experiment 2 still failed at roughly 9.4-9.9 cm and -123 to -128 degrees plus an 18.2 cm/-154.8 degree case. Detailed researcher-evaluation artifacts show that most retained-policy failures have maximum hold counts of zero or two steps and minimum distances close to the 1 cm boundary, whereas fresh failures are broad and often never approach the target. The current 11-value observation contains joint state, Cartesian error, both inverse-kinematics branch errors, direct two-joint actions, and saved normalization, so transfer is semantically compatible, not merely dimension-compatible. The lower learning rate preserved behavior but did not reduce residual count. In experiment 10, training success fell from 1.00 at the early measured checkpoint to about 0.68-0.69 later while mean reward rose; the queried log also shows changing PPO statistics during this decline, but the measured policy only partially recovered late. This is another training/task discrepancy, not evidence of task progress. Fixed 200-episode panels are development evidence rather than the official final assessment.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether near-boundary failures are limited by action-level control, PPO update dynamics, or the learned policy class after the tested reward-curvature intervention failed to improve the retained trajectory. Transfer history and seed-dependent optimization remain confounded by the two poor fresh replications. It is also unknown how well either development panel predicts the official final assessment. The evidence does not yet distinguish whether changing rollout aggregation can stabilize transfer without sacrificing the learned reaching behavior. No open question is a prescribed next action.
